rationale:
ROUND 3. Round 2 returned REVISE, gated by `bug_historian`, and its objection is the exact continuation of its round-1 one — which is the strongest argument that the seat is tracking something real rather than restating a preference.

THE OBJECTION: I had wired the durable drop-record into `ValidateSitePlanAction` only, while `apply_gap_plan_action.go`'s three call sites share the SAME resolver and lost names exactly as silently. The seat is right, and the scoping was worse than it looked: content-gap-planner runs **116 orchestrations/30d** against build-site-planner's handful, so the class fix was aimed at the quieter of the two paths.

FIXED (commit 0b39f5a99). All FOUR drop sites now file a durable `PLAN_SECTION_NAME_DROPPED` finding. The three gap-plan sites take (ctx, db, siteID, logger) and no ActionParams — and six other lanes' tests call them directly, so widening those signatures would collide rather than help — so they use a sibling recorder that names its provenance EXPLICITLY (agent_type, action) instead of inheriting it. That is the stricter half of the rule editquality raised in round 2: an entry whose provenance was never stated is one the writer's merge can fill for you. Validate keeps the INHERITING door deliberately, because a drop there genuinely belongs to the running step. Both choices are now asserted by tests rather than described.

THE OTHER ROUND-2 OBJECTIONS.
(1) bug_historian LOW, the swallowed error — `attempted, _ := LogActionFindings(...)` meant a failed record was itself silent, the same shape one level up. It cannot be made fatal: the findings door is best-effort by design, and failing a plan because its REPORT failed is worse than the thing being reported. So `warnUnrecordedDrops` makes the shortfall loud. Tested with zaptest/observer, including the nil-logger path.
(2) editquality MEDIUM, provenance — answered above; the assertion matches agent_type/action/error_code/severity on the row itself, and a mutation deleting the stated agent_type fails it.
(3) editquality LOW + guardian MEDIUM, volume on `agent_error_log` — MEASURED, not argued: the table already takes **12,012 rows in 7 days** (10,080 of them error_code UNKNOWN), and gap-plan applies run 116/30d. Even if every single run dropped a name — they do not; a drop is the exception — this adds **under 0.2%** of existing volume, into a table whose whole purpose is durable findings.
(4) debug_historian MEDIUM, post-deploy verification — the lane RUNBOOK now carries it, corrected earlier today after its first recipe FAILED ITS OWN CONTROL: probing `/proc/1/exe` for this lane's sha returned absent, and so did a commit already proven live on the running image, because the binary carries only the ONE commit it was built at. The working method is an ordering proof (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` against a known-live commit, plus the deployed tag and makefile IMAGE_TAG), and it currently shows the Go half is definitively not live.
(5) guardian/debug_historian LOW on migration 439's WHERE clause — re-verified at review time: exactly ONE active non-snapshot build-site-planner row (version 1), `output_field` top-level (`available_components`, config-nested path NULL). The DO-block's count(*)=1 RAISE fires inside the transaction, so a second row aborts the apply rather than half-writing it.

MUTATION FOUND THE SAME GAP AGAIN, ONE LEVEL OUT — and this is worth recording as the round's real finding. Deleting the recorder call from `applyNewPage` left every existing gap-plan test GREEN: the suite was silent about the new wiring exactly as it had been about validate's in round 2. A wiring test at that site now fails under that mutation. Seven mutations, all biting; whole package suite green; clean-tree `git archive HEAD` build green.

UNCHANGED FROM ROUNDS 1-2: the core mechanism and every reason for it — the acceptance surface consumes the offer's OUTPUT rather than re-deriving a predicate that lives in config and has already drifted (419 edited 407's query); UNION never removal; opt-in with the unsafe default OFF; the shared resolver's DB query and signature untouched, so no path gains the authority PLAN-049 withheld from it; order-safe in both deploy directions.

plan.summary: ROUND 3. Unchanged core (opt-in `menu_field` lets validate accept the component menu its own planner step was shown) plus the class closure the council gated on: ALL FOUR sites that drop a section name through loadComponentNameResolver — validate_site_plan and apply_gap_plan's three — now file a durable PLAN_SECTION_NAME_DROPPED finding, the gap-plan ones naming their provenance explicitly; a record that fails to write is warned about rather than swallowed. Migration 439 (applied) opts in build-site-planner only.

edits.rationale: New file, not a hunk in v3_site_actions.go: that file is edited by several sessions concurrently (it was dirty from another lane this morning) and a same-file passenger cannot be prevented by any pathspec. addMenu UNIONs menu rows into validFunctions/nameToFunc/displayToFunc with the DB base winning on identity collisions; menuRowsFrom refuses anything that is not a non-empty []interface{} so a misconfigured path degrades to today's behaviour rather than to a resolver that accepts ""; resolvedViaMenu exists so a run can SAY the arm fired.

Two minimal hunks. The struct gains menuOnly (attribution only). The call site reads the opt-in key and logs both the arm firing and, per resolved section, whether it owes acceptance to the menu — without that tell, 'the widening reached the plan' and 'the planner proposed nothing from the widened class' are indistinguishable in the logs and in site_plan_sections.

407's idiom: snapshot_agent, jsonb_set, DO-block guard that RAISEs. The guard checks BOTH halves together — menu_field must equal load_components.output_field — because a menu_field naming a path no step writes is the one way this change can be inert while looking applied, which is bugs_open/282 itself one level up. ROLLBACK sidecar removes the key, which is a complete revert whether or not the Go has rolled.

The resolver had ZERO test coverage before this (grep of *_test.go for loadComponentNameResolver: no hits), which is part of why a whole class of names could vanish unnoticed. Nine tests: menu function resolves and is attributed; display-name echo resolves; base identity wins a collision; malformed rows add nothing and never make "" valid; shape variance on the collected-data path; and two sqlmock action-level tests — WITH menu_field the tool section survives, WITHOUT it the identical plan still drops it (the un-opted-in control).

edits.rationale: ROUND 2, answering bug_historian's HIGH. A drop was previously a Warn and nothing else — the estate's most-repeated failure shape (content silently lost in a plan pass, discovered only after damage). Now every drop files a durable agenterrors Finding through LogActionFindings, the door this action already uses for recordRecomposeOutcomes, with the same 'warning' severity and the same reasoning (a drop is a legal outcome; invisibility is not). Applies to EVERY caller, including the un-opted-in ones the scoping decision leaves on the old behaviour, so their exposure is now visible rather than implied. droppedRemedy/droppedFindings are pure so the record's shape is assertable without a database; recordDroppedSectionNames returns its attempted count because a mock cannot prove the negative case.

ROUND 3, answering bug_historian's round-2 HIGH. These three share loadComponentNameResolver with validate and dropped unresolved names with a Warn and nothing else — on the fleet's DOMINANT placement path (content-gap-planner, 116 runs/30d). Each now collects its drops and calls the shared recorder. Signatures are deliberately unchanged (six other lanes' tests call these directly), so provenance is stated explicitly rather than inherited.
